# flightdeck_teamspace_project (Resource)

Says that a Flightdeck teamspace owns a project. A project can belong to more than one team, and the link shows the project's name on the team's page to everyone in the workspace.

Linking or unlinking a project needs a workspace member who is not a guest, with both **read** and **administer** on that project. With the built-in roles that is the project's admins, and a workspace owner or admin on every project. A project the token cannot see is refused the same way as an id that names no project, so the error cannot tell you which. Linking a project that is already linked adopts that link rather than failing, so destroying this resource unlinks it even if it was linked some other way. Changing either id replaces the link.

Import with `<teamspace_id>/<project_id>`: `terraform import flightdeck_teamspace_project.app 12/42`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "flightdeck_project" "app" {
  name       = "Mobile App"
  identifier = "APP"
}

resource "flightdeck_teamspace" "platform" {
  name = "Platform"
}

# The team owns the project. The token needs read and administer on the
# project to link it.
resource "flightdeck_teamspace_project" "app" {
  teamspace_id = flightdeck_teamspace.platform.id
  project_id   = flightdeck_project.app.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (Number) Id of the project the team owns. Changing it replaces the link.
- `teamspace_id` (Number) Id of the teamspace. Changing it replaces the link.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<teamspace_id>/<project_id>`, the import id. A link has no id of its own.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with <teamspace_id>/<project_id>.
terraform import flightdeck_teamspace_project.app 12/42
```
